item.title: Weil Gotshal Collapse: Is This Big Law’s Lehman Moment?
item.description: Weil’s collapse has us wondering whether lawyers are the new bankers.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: China Shock Is Harder to Fight for Thailand With the Superpower Next Door
item.description: After a lean few years, Thailand’s economy is showing signs of improvement. Deflation has given way to inflation of almost 3%, while policymakers are upgrading growth forecasts. With the recovery still modest, however, officials have little reason to rush: Absent a major upheaval, they can take their time lifting interest rates from historically low levels.It's an encouraging picture — but one that tells only part of the story.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss

item.title: Grand Theft Auto May Be Outdated in the AI Video Game Age
item.description: Video games need AI not just to fix the industry’s economics, but to usher in a new era of creativity.
item.dc:creator: Gearoid Reidy

item.title: Run on the Law Firm
item.description: Weil Gotshal, bankers turned lawyers, onion protests, more sports bets.
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine

item.title: South Korea’s Military Ambitions Get a Reality Check
item.description: The deck is stacked against a significant shift in military control on the Korean Peninsula, yet that is exactly what South Korean President Lee Jae Myung is staking his leadership on. It’s the right idea, at the wrong time.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Pollard

item.title: Troy Aikman’s ESPN Contract Dispute Shows NFL Broadcasting Is Changing
item.description: Troy Aikman’s $18 million-a-year ESPN contract expires after February’s Super Bowl, and speculation about what’s next has become a high-dollar soap opera. His longtime broadcast partner, Joe Buck, recently secured a six-year extension reportedly worth $108 million, while Aikman remains unsigned. The two even reportedly argued about their contracts before a recent game.
item.dc:creator: Adam Minter

item.title: Weil Gotshal & Manges: Weil Collapse Shows Lawyers Are the New Bankers
item.description: The implosion of US law firm Weil Gotshal & Manges, whose elite restructuring experts once advised on Lehman Brothers’ collapse, confirms that lawyers really are the new bankers — massive pay checks and destabilizing bank runs included.
item.dc:creator: Chris Bryant

item.title: Britain’s Budget Sugar Rush Will Wear Off Rapidly by 2027
item.description: Looking for a way to placate demanding kids while money’s tight? Try pick’n’mix. John Healey has done exactly that in his first budget as Britain’s chancellor of the exchequer. He delivered 98 new policy measures — lots of little sweet treats, at a reasonable price. The last time there were so many items in this yearly event was back in 2010, and this latest batch costs a lot less on average (as a percentage of gross domestic product).
item.dc:creator: Mihir Sharma

item.title: Alphabet Earnings: Google Parent's Wobbly Quarter Is No Sign of a Crisis
item.description: Investors were thoroughly unimpressed with Alphabet Inc.’s third-quarter earnings on Wednesday evening. Shares tumbled nearly 11% after the company missed sales and profit expectations. It was a sign, Bloomberg News reported, that Wall Street wasn’t satisfied that Google is seeing enough of a return on its artificial-intelligence bets.
item.dc:creator: Dave Lee

item.title: Republicans Have a Problem With Young Men. Vance Is Not the Answer
item.description: Remember July 2024 when former pro wrestler Hulk Hogan stood on stage at the RNC convention? He ripped his shirt in half to reveal a red Trump-Vance tank top and yelled “let Trumpamania run wild, brother!”
item.dc:creator: Nia-Malika Henderson

item.title: France’s Debt Reckoning Is a Peek Into America’s Future
item.description: Many long simmering tensions boiled over in France’s protests and riots. Rising borrowing costs for the government proved a crucial pressure point — a message from bondholders grown impatient with a lack of pension reform and the country’s enormous welfare state. Americans would do well to pay attention.
item.dc:creator: Allison Schrager

item.title: Russia's Plague Scare Highlights Need for Lab Safety, Biosecurity
item.description: Too much remains unknown about the death of Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old lab technician for a Russian research institute. Her employer has denied local media reports that she may have been exposed to plague after breaking a test tube. Russian officials, who say no cases of plague have been reported in the region, have attributed her death to pneumonia.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Machado Must Embrace Patience to Secure Venezuela’s Political Future
item.description: María Corina Machado’s return to Venezuela has some of the same sweep and drama of Simón Bolivar’s return more than two centuries ago. But if she wants her story to end better than one of the great heroic deeds of 19th-century Latin America, she will have to match her passion for her nation with patience for change.
item.dc:creator: Juan Pablo Spinetto

item.title: Trump’s Latin America Winning Streak Ends in Brazil
item.description: The “Donroe Doctrine” — President Donald Trump’s effort to reforge the Western Hemisphere under US leadership — has been the most consistent, and most successful, aspect of his statecraft. That geopolitical gambit has both benefited from and helped catalyze Latin America’s swing to the political right.
item.dc:creator: Hal Brands

item.title: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s AI Optimism Risks Policy Choices
item.description: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh champions parsimony in central bank communications and loathes so-called forward guidance. But he’s said plenty about the future of artificial intelligence: He’s an arch optimist on the technology who thinks it will help him vanquish inflation. item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: French Debt's Riot Premium Is a Test for Le Pen
item.description: If the bond market could talk, it might respond to France’s increased policing after recent riots with the words of the crusader knight from the Indiana Jones series: “You have chosen… wisely.”
item.dc:creator: Lionel Laurent

item.title: Fed Rates: Lord, Let Me Hike, Just Not Now
item.description: Warsh sidesteps the midterms elephant in the room.
item.dc:creator: John Authers
